turns.reply: Hi there! How can I help you with your knowledge graph today?

I am NodeSpace's built-in assistant, and I help you work with your knowledge graph. My core functions include:

*   **Creating Nodes:** Adding new pieces of information (instances) or defining entirely new types of things to track (**schemas**) using `create_node` or `create_schema`.
*   **Finding/Listing Data:** Searching for specific nodes by keyword (`search_nodes`), finding related concepts semantically (`search_semantic`), getting the full details of a known node ID (`get_node`), or listing everything under an existing type.
*   **Updating Information:** Modifying content or properties on existing nodes (`update_node`) or changing task statuses specifically (`update_task_status`).
*   **Structuring Knowledge:** Defining relationships between different kinds of data points with `create_relationship`, and modifying your tracking structures themselves via `update_schema`.

Essentially, I help you build out, organize, read from, and modify structured knowledge within our graph!

supersedes: e4b-decontaminated (9/12 raw, 8 effective); superseded by the runner from #1778
note: Measured after the #1775 argument-error-reporting fix, rebased onto the shared eval runner (#1778), on a purged DB with a daemon rebuilt from this commit and the preflight gate passing. Raw 8/12. THREE runs of this work exist and they disagree: 10/12, 9/12, 8/12, on code that differs only by the title_template addition between runs 1-2 and 3. Read the per-scenario traces, not the count. The one durable, verified change is that unparseable tool arguments are now reported as such - visible in this run's log for both create_schema and create_node - where the harness previously substituted {} and produced a misleading missing-required-field error. Scenario 3 remains a FALSE PASS and scenario 4 still cascades from it; this work did NOT fix that. Run 3 additionally surfaced a cross-turn duplicate write that the earlier runs did not (caveats[2]).
caveats: Scenario 3 is a FALSE PASS in all three runs and #1775 did NOT fix it. The model calls create_schema with a title_template and NO fields array ({"name":"Equipment Check-out Tracker","title_template":"{equipment} ({status})"}), which is rejected. The noExtraTypes assertion only checks that create_schema was called once, so it cannot see that nothing persisted. The error now names every unresolved placeholder at once and prescribes the exact entries to add, and the model STILL does not repair it: in runs 2 and 3 its retry emitted create_schema with EMPTY arguments. In run 3 it then created an unrelated fields-less 'checkout-log' schema instead. Better error text was necessary but is not sufficient for this model on this shape.

Scenario 4 fails in all three runs, downstream of scenario 3 - there is no equipment type to instantiate. The acceptance criterion 'an instance request against an existing schema calls create_node' is therefore NOT demonstrated by scenario 4 in any run. 8c/8d exercise it against types that do exist.

NEW in run 3, not seen in runs 1-2: a CROSS-TURN duplicate write. 8c completed correctly (one create_node, node f1f25564, reply 'I have added Kind of Blue'). Then 8d's turn re-executed the PREVIOUS turn's instruction, calling create_node for 'Kind of Blue by Miles Davis' again at its iteration 1 (node 0bbcb76b) before creating the Blue Note venue. Two nodes now exist for one request. The duplicate-call guard in agent_loop.rs cannot catch this: seen_calls is per-turn and is reset between turns, by design. The eval scrapes tool calls per chat node, so 8d's stray call is attributed to 8c's assertion too, which is why BOTH report 'got 2' from a single extra write. This is a real defect and a DIFFERENT one from what #1775 fixed - it is a cross-turn instruction-repetition bug, not an argument-construction or error-reporting bug. Filed as #1780.

Scenario 8c's status across runs: PASSED in runs 1 and 2, FAILED in run 3 - and the run-3 failure is caused by the cross-turn duplicate above, not by a regression in the argument-error fix. In all three runs the underlying argument error is now reported correctly ('The arguments for create_node were not valid JSON...'), which is the change this issue set out to make; run 3's log shows the model recovering from exactly that message and creating the node successfully on its next call.

Run-to-run variance is large and measured. Across three runs: scenario 5 flipped twice (pass/fail/pass), 8c and 8d flipped in run 3. A single-run delta of 1-2 on this matrix is noise. Do not use the headline count to judge a change; use per-scenario tool traces and the daemon log.
Scenario 6 (update) fails in all three runs and is owned by #1637, out of scope here.

Still not exercised by any run: the within-array field locating that is the largest part of the #1775 change. No create_schema call in any run sent a malformed entry inside a fields array - the shape from ~/.nodespace/logs/nodespaced.log lines 130-162 - so that path is covered by unit tests only.
effective_note: 8/12 raw minus scenario 3, a confirmed false pass whose create_schema failed and persisted nothing. Prior recorded effective was 8; the drop is the run-3 cross-turn duplicate (caveats[2]), a newly surfaced defect, not a regression from this fix.
